goalbuddy_receipt_v1.rationale: T019 closes every T018 graph blocker. The remote test now independently hashes stored records, clears its state, and proves exact canonical snapshot/hash recovery. Missing and mismatched acknowledgements both remain degraded without checkpoints. Closure preflight permits only identity-exact replay and rejects competing or dual-classified closures before commit. Separate tests prove successful authenticated, parameterized direct-Neo4j fallback for malformed and thrown Graphiti project/query failures, with shared canonical filtering. The focused suite passes 16/16, Codex verification and diff hygiene pass, and T019 reports all broad verifiers green. The temporal graph milestone is ready for the bounded ontology/improve slice; the overall goal remains incomplete.

worker_package.objective: Implement T006 as one executable ontology-and-continuous-improvement vertical slice over canonical episodes, admission policy, and the temporal graph. Add an encrypted, immutable, workspace-scoped ontology registry with deterministic change/version IDs and states core|shadow|active|deprecated|quarantined|rejected. Permit only additive shadow→active promotion after all configured gates pass: structural/backward compatibility, default support from at least three independent currently admitted claims, scope/collision checks, and deterministic retrieval-evaluation improvement without regression; each promotion creates a new immutable version. Rename, merge, delete, narrowing, or other destructive changes must remain quarantined and must not alter active validation or graph projection. Add an idempotent memory-improve worker with per-workspace high-watermarks and independently injected extractor/verifier identities; missing, failed, dependent, or unverified verifier output must never activate claims. Resolve explicit aliases deterministically while preserving incompatible homonyms, route conflicts and temporal replacements through graph preflight/admission, revalidate TTL claims, and isolate workspace failures. Produce rebuildable cited enrichment projections for triplets, embeddings, communities, and summaries, each bound to source claims, episodes, evidence, admissions, and ontology version; tombstones/revocations must remove their authority before projection cleanup. Implement bounded feedback weights that cannot change admission, claim status, ontology state, or tombstones. Add idempotent session-close notification and consolidation that completes within 120 seconds under a healthy deterministic fixture. Acceptance is executable KG-AC10/11 and IM-AC01/02/03 coverage plus an end-to-end canonical episode→independent verification/admission→entity/conflict resolution→graph/enrichment→replay scenario. Keep new behavior explicitly invoked/disabled by default; do not implement router, MCP/API recall, deployment, live services, or configuration migration.
verify: node --test tests/memory-improve-worker.test.mjs tests/ontology-registry.test.mjs tests/knowledge-graph-adapter.test.mjs tests/memory-admission-policy.test.mjs tests/codex-working-set-store.test.mjs tests/codex-working-memory-integration.test.mjs
stop_if: Any required change falls outside allowed_files or requires router, MCP/API recall, daemon deployment, Portainer, configuration migration, live credentials, network access, or a real user vault.
An extractor can verify its own output, verifier independence cannot be established, or missing/failed verification can activate or project a claim.
An ontology extension can activate without compatibility, independent-support, scope/collision, and deterministic evaluation gates, or activation mutates an existing ontology version.
A rename, merge, delete, narrowing, or other destructive ontology mutation can alter active validation or graph state instead of remaining quarantined.
A shadow or quarantined type becomes queryable/projectable as active, or historical graph records lose their original ontology-version binding.
Replaying a job or session-close notification duplicates a claim, entity, relation, ontology change/version, enrichment artifact, or durable checkpoint.
One workspace's failed job blocks another workspace, crosses scope, or advances the failed workspace high-watermark past unprocessed canonical episodes.
Feedback can activate, delete, tombstone, revoke, or change the admission/ontology authority of a claim, or its weight is not deterministically bounded.
A tombstoned episode or revoked/expired admission can retain authoritative summaries, embeddings, communities, or feedback-influenced results.
The healthy deterministic session-close fixture cannot complete consolidation within 120 seconds of the close timestamp.
The same verification failure remains unresolved after two attempts.

evidence: T020 reran the graph/ontology suite: 16 tests passed with zero failures, including explicit closure-collision, remote rebuild, hash-acknowledgement, fallback, atomicity, and workspace-safety cases.

The stateful remote fixture independently hashes copied canonical projection records, supports complete loss, and exactly matches canonical state after rebuild.
Separate tests prove omitted and deliberately incorrect projection hashes produce projected=false and no checkpoint directory.
Malformed and thrown Graphiti cases separately reach authenticated, parameterized direct Neo4j fallback with canonical filtering.

parallel_safety.rationale: Ontology versions, improve checkpoints, graph validation, canonical episode consumption, and shared acceptance tests define one authority chain and overlap; one Worker must own the slice.
